citations.title: National Grid Announces Zoe Yujnovich as New Chief Executive, Shares Slide

sentences.quote: Yujnovich, who most recently served as Integrated Gas and Upstream Director at Shell, will join the National Grid Board as Chief Executive Designate on 1 September and formally take over on 17 November.
sentences.text: Zoe Yujnovich became chief executive of National Grid plc on 17 November 2025, having joined the board as chief executive designate on 1 September 2025, succeeding John Pettigrew, who retired after nearly a decade in the role.

She joined from Shell, where she was Integrated Gas and Upstream Director and held various senior roles since 2014, and before that spent almost two decades at Rio Tinto, including as President and Chief Executive Officer of the Iron Ore Company of Canada.
She began her career at Rio Tinto as an engineer and has worked in Australia, Brazil, Canada, the Netherlands, the United States and the United Kingdom.
She is also a non-executive director of Unilever plc and holds a Bachelor of Engineering (Hons) from the University of Western Australia and an Executive MBA from the University of Utah.

sentences.quote: National Grid plc (LSE: NG.) will reduce its Group Executive Committee from 13 members to eight and reorganise operational responsibility around single presidents for the United Kingdom and United States from September 1, 2026.
sentences.text: In August 2026 National Grid announced a streamlined structure effective 1 September 2026, cutting the executive committee from 13 members to eight and placing each geography under one leader: Cordi O'Hara as President UK, covering electricity distribution and transmission, and Sally Librera as interim President US pending an internal and external search.

sentences.quote: Carl Trowell has been appointed President of Global Capital, with responsibility for improving delivery against budget and schedule across National Grid's expanding investment programme. Alice Delahunty will become Chief Technology and Innovation Officer
sentences.text: Carl Trowell was appointed President of Global Capital and Alice Delahunty Chief Technology and Innovation Officer.

sentences.quote: Chief executive Zoe Yujnovich said the group's commitment to invest at least GBP 70 billion in modernising and expanding energy networks across the UK and the US Northeast required "absolute clarity of accountability and a relentless focus on performance".
sentences.text: Yujnovich said the commitment to invest at least 70 billion pounds required clear accountability and focus on performance.

citations.title: National Grid Appoints Zoe Yujnovich as New Chief Executive to Lead the Next Phase of Growth

sentences.quote: Zoe will assume the position of Chief Executive Designate on 1 September 2025 and will officially take on the role of Chief Executive on 17 November 2025.
sentences.text: Zoe Yujnovich became chief executive in November 2025, succeeding John Pettigrew, who retired after nearly 10 years in the role; she joined from Shell, where she was director of Integrated Gas and Upstream, and earlier worked at Rio Tinto, including as chief executive of its iron ore company in Canada.
FY2025/26 brought record capital investment of GBP 11.6bn, asset growth of 10.9% and a total dividend of 48.49p, up 3.8%, with underlying earnings per share up 8% at constant currency.
Net debt rose to GBP 44.2bn, with GBP 2.8bn of proceeds from the National Grid Renewables and Grain LNG divestments partly offsetting higher capex.
Around two-thirds of the at least GBP 70bn investment plan is covered by regulatory agreements, including the RIIO-T3 price control.

sentences.text: National Grid plans at least GBP 70 billion of capital investment over the five years from 2026/27 to 2030/31, targeting asset growth of around 10% CAGR and underlying EPS CAGR of 8-10% from a 2025/26 baseline of 78.0p.

sentences.quote: Around two-thirds of this programme is already covered by regulatory agreements, and about three-quarters of delivery mechanisms are secured, supporting visibility.
sentences.text: Visibility is relatively high, as about two-thirds of the programme is already covered by regulatory agreements and roughly three-quarters of delivery mechanisms are secured.

Spending is split across two regulated regions, with around GBP 17 billion planned in New York and GBP 12 billion in New England, and the US regulated asset base expected to grow about 50% over five years to more than GBP 45 billion.
